overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the notice listed the parties, address and topic, so the Commission's MOU vote naturally flowed from the posted discussion.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the October 2 notice was insufficient because the MOU topic sat under 'Business,' where votes are not typically taken, so it did not signal a vote.
allegations.key_passage: It is reasonably foreseeable that a public body may take action and hold a vote following discussion of a topic listed on a meeting notice; the Open Meeting Law does not require that the notice separately indicate the possibility of a vote.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
